subject: Music Production
title: The Bomb Squad's Wall of Sound
description: A quick, practical guide to The Bomb Squad's Wall of Sound.

hook.text: Public Enemy's production team, The Bomb Squad, layered dozens of samples into a single track.

buildup.text: Their 1988 album 'It Takes a Nation of Millions' stacked sirens, funk, and noise into dense collages.

discovery.text: This chaotic layering created a sonic wall that was aggressive, political, and unlike anything before.

twist.text: Today this album could not be made because clearing dozens of samples per track would cost millions.

climax.text: The Bomb Squad's work showed that sampling could be a radical art form, not just borrowing.

punchline.text: Dozens of samples per track built hip-hop's densest sound.

quiz.question: Why couldn't The Bomb Squad's album be easily replicated today?
options: Clearing dozens of samples per track would cost millions
